title: Friday, August 28, 2026

headline.title: Chair Warsh delivers his first Jackson Hole keynote at 9:00am CT — the first policy framing from a new Fed Chair rather than a restatement of a known one. July core PCE is stuck at 3.3% with headline at 3.7%, two Fed officials have already called inflation too hot, and roughly a third of bond traders are pricing a September hike. Warsh has deliberately reduced forward guidance, so anything he says on inflation, productivity, the balance sheet or the conditions for another hike is potentially market-moving. Chicago PMI 8:45am CT, final Michigan sentiment 9:00am. The Nasdaq is the clear laggard into it, futures −0.29% against a Dow fractionally positive, with the 10-year +2bps to 4.69%.
headline.summary: The tape is genuinely two-sided into it. MRVL is −8.5% despite a record $2.74B quarter and an a raise of both its FY2027 and FY2028 revenue outlooks on strong AI bookings. EPS $0.94 beat $0.93 and revenue rose 37% to $2.739B. The stock is up 184% this year — that is the whole story. Non-GAAP gross margin guided 57.5-58.5% against a 58.5% consensus, and limited new detail on the Google opportunity disappointed. A pure expectations gap. PYPL is −15.7% after a reported $60.50-a-share, ~$53B Advent/Stripe-led approach was rejected by the board, erasing the deal premium built since July. On the other side, ESTC +17.8%, AFRM +13.0% and UMC +10.1% lead. Semis are giving back Thursday’s rip — MU −1.9%, INTC −2.1%, SMH −0.9%.

Be in position before 9:00am, at 8:50-8:55am, because the new 6HR candle opens at 9:00 and the break is taken then. If it happens great, if not we move on.

darkpool.note: Thursday’s board flipped to heavily ask-side on mega-cap tech and semis, the mirror image of Wednesday’s bid-side stacking. The largest single-name print was MSFT $841M on the ask after hours, and cumulative flow ran NVDA $8.3B ask out front, then SPY $5.0B ask, MU $4.1B ask and MSFT $3.3B ask. On the ETF side VOO $958M on the ask topped the entire board as the single largest print, with IVV $763M ask and short-duration Treasuries VGSH $684M ask behind it — benchmark and rate money repositioning directly into the Fed’s main event. Both of the loudest options tickets were calls: an NEE $40C 01/15/27 block at $417.3M, the biggest single options ticket on the board by a wide margin, and an NVDA $200C 01/15/27 sweep at $56.6M. Constructive footprints, but that is two prints, not the whole tape, into a speech nobody has heard before.
